minutes.headline: Finance Committee backed most FY24 warrant articles and deferred the capital plan, senior tax relief and the historic survey.
minutes.summary: The committee held its public hearing on the annual town meeting warrant. The town manager presented revenues, free cash uses, health insurance increases and the capital plan, and the Select Board and Personnel Committee presented their articles. Most articles were recommended unanimously; several were deferred pending wording changes or removal.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to recommend approval of the omnibus budget article for FY24, unanimously.
The committee deferred its vote on the FY24 capital plan article to a following meeting.
The committee recommended deferral of the senior tax exemption petition, and that article is to return with reworded sections.
The committee recommended deferral of the historic homes survey until its language is fixed, and also of the TIF agreement and public safety building security articles.
The committee recommended approval of the free cash deposits to stabilization, special purpose stabilization and the OPEB trust, each unanimously.

why_it_matters: The omnibus budget and the free cash deposits are what town meeting will be asked to vote on, and they set a large part of the town budget, mostly taxes.

Deferring the capital plan, senior tax relief and the TIF agreement means these articles reach residents with the committee's position still unsettled, and the senior relief mechanism shifts part of the cost to other taxpayers' bills.
watch_next: The committee's next meeting on the sixth, when the town meeting report is to be finished and voted on.
The return of the senior tax relief article with reworded preamble and section six, and the deferred capital plan vote.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on nearly every Article A–Z vote and on the main dollar figures; the differences are mostly mishearings of names and digits. The one thing to know is that ours could not hear the outcome of Articles I and N, and that the official minutes record warrant removals (Articles H, O, U, V) and a $4,127,165.91 transfer total that ours does not, while ours lists seven line-item transfers the official minutes never itemize.
